free_text.inst.v2.D8: The clearest miss is health. The plain reading puts 'your health and energy' in the list of matters that read well, and lists it again as 'live right now' -- for a man whose documented life, from 1984 until his death in 2016, was thirty-two years with a diagnosed movement disorder that took his speech and mobility, that is close to the opposite of what actually happened. It also files 'courage, and brothers and sisters' under matters that read hard. His documented courage is one of the best-attested things about him -- giving up his title and facing a felony conviction in 1967 rather than accept induction -- and his one brother, Rahaman, stayed close to him his whole life; the record does not support 'hard' on either count. The same house problem shows up with income: 'income, gains and friends' is called hard, but the documented purses from his fights were enormous, so that reads flatly wrong too. The one place the text is specific rather than generic -- it flags itself as unusually positive about luck -- lines up better: an Olympic gold at eighteen, a stripped title returned by a unanimous Supreme Court reversal in 1971, and a comeback that produced two more reigns as champion is a documented run of good luck, so I'll credit that one. Higher study is also called unusually favourable, but the record (limited formal schooling, reported reading difficulty, no education past high school) does not back that up. Overall: one specific claim landed, one specific claim missed, and the two vaguest, most consequential claims -- health and courage -- were wrong in a way that matters.
